question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The annual fiscal report was severely criticized by the opposition. || II. The finance minister had to issue a public clarification. || Starters: A. Having severely criticized... B. Having been severely criticized... C. Following the severe criticism of... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'Having been severely criticized by the opposition, the annual fiscal report required the finance minister to issue a public clarification.' 2) 'Following the severe criticism of the annual fiscal report by the opposition, the finance minister had to issue a public clarification.' Agar hum Starter A ('Having severely criticized') use karte hain, toh dangling modifier ban jata hai kyunki lagta hai Finance Minister ne report ko criticize kiya, jo logically galat hai.
trick: 'Having + V3' active voice hai. Yahan report criticize hui thi (passive), isliye 'Having been' aayega.
tip: Hamesha check karein ki participle ke baad aane wala subject action se match kare.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The industrial effluents were consistently discharged into the river. || II. The local authorities imposed a heavy penalty on the factory. || Starters: A. Discharging the industrial effluents... B. On account of the consistent discharge of... C. Imposing a heavy penalty... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'On account of the consistent discharge of industrial effluents into the river, the local authorities imposed a heavy penalty.' 2) 'Imposing a heavy penalty on the factory, the local authorities reacted to the consistent discharge of effluents.' Starter A galat hai kyunki 'Discharging' se sentence shuru karne par lagta hai ki local authorities effluents discharge kar rahi thi (dangling modifier).
trick: Starter C main clause ke subject (local authorities) ke action (imposing) ko perfectly describe karta hai.
tip: V+ing starter wahi lega jo action sach mein kar raha ho.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The sovereign bonds offered lucrative interest rates. || II. Foreign institutional investors pumped billions into the domestic market. || Starters: A. Enticed by the lucrative interest rates... B. Offering lucrative interest rates... C. As the sovereign bonds offered... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'Enticed by the lucrative interest rates offered by the sovereign bonds, foreign institutional investors pumped billions.' 2) 'As the sovereign bonds offered lucrative interest rates, foreign institutional investors pumped billions.' Starter B ek dangling modifier trap hai kyunki ise investors ke sath lagane par meaning nikalta hai ki investors interest rates offer kar rahe the.
trick: Sentence ka doer identify karein. Bonds offer kar rahe hain, investors entice ho rahe hain.
tip: Cause and effect ka logical order kabhi change nahi hona chahiye.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The archaic labor laws were successfully overhauled by the parliament. || II. The manufacturing sector witnessed a sudden surge in foreign investments. || Starters: A. Having been successfully overhauled... B. Witnessing a sudden surge in... C. Despite overhauling the archaic... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'Having been successfully overhauled by the parliament, the archaic labor laws caused a sudden surge in foreign investments.' 2) 'Witnessing a sudden surge in foreign investments, the manufacturing sector benefited from the successfully overhauled labor laws.' Starter C galat hai kyunki 'Despite' meaning ko contradict karta hai (positive action ka negative result dikhata hai).
trick: Conjunctions jaise 'Despite' sirf contrasting sentences ko jodne ke liye use hote hain.
tip: Passive structures ('Having been') hamesha non-living subjects ke liye check karein.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The telecom sector faces a severe liquidity crunch. || II. Several mid-sized operators are planning to merge. || Starters: A. Facing a severe liquidity crunch... B. To face a severe liquidity... C. Driven by a severe liquidity crunch... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'Facing a severe liquidity crunch, several mid-sized telecom operators are planning to merge.' 2) 'Driven by a severe liquidity crunch, several mid-sized operators in the telecom sector are planning to merge.' Starter B ('To face') ek infinitive purpose dikhata hai, jo yahan illogical hai kyunki operators intentionally liquidity crunch face nahi karna chahte.
trick: 'To + V1' hamesha future purpose ya intention dikhata hai, current majboori nahi.
tip: Infinitive starters purpose batate hain, cause-effect nahi.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The monsoon arrived earlier than expected this year. || II. The agricultural output is projected to hit a record high. || Starters: A. Having arrived earlier than expected... B. Projecting to hit a record high... C. With the monsoon arriving earlier... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'Having arrived earlier than expected, the monsoon caused the agricultural output to be projected at a record high.' 2) 'With the monsoon arriving earlier than expected, the agricultural output is projected to hit a record high.' Starter B galat hai kyunki monsoon khud kuch 'project' nahi kar raha hai, yeh data analysts ka kaam hai.
trick: Absolute phrase ('With + noun + participle') cause-effect batane ka sabse safe tarika hota hai.
tip: Prepositional phrases hamesha independent clauses ko smoothly jodte hain.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The artificial intelligence algorithms were poorly optimized. || II. The server farm consumed unprecedented amounts of electricity. || Starters: A. Being poorly optimized... B. Consuming unprecedented amounts of... C. Having optimized poorly... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'Being poorly optimized, the artificial intelligence algorithms caused the server farm to consume unprecedented electricity.' 2) 'Consuming unprecedented amounts of electricity, the server farm struggled due to the poorly optimized algorithms.' Starter C ek grammatical error hai kyunki 'Having optimized' active hai, jabki algorithms khud ko optimize nahi karte (passive chaiye tha).
trick: 'Being + V3' state of being dikhata hai, jo poorly optimized algorithms ke liye perfect hai.
tip: Active aur passive voice ka difference sentence ka meaning badal deta hai.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The supreme court issued a landmark verdict on digital privacy. || II. Many tech giants are scrambling to update their terms of service. || Starters: A. Following the landmark verdict issued... B. Scrambling to update their terms... C. Having issued a landmark verdict... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'Following the landmark verdict issued by the supreme court, many tech giants are scrambling to update their terms.' 2) 'Scrambling to update their terms of service, many tech giants are reacting to the supreme court verdict.' Starter C dangling modifier banata hai kyunki tech giants ne verdict issue nahi kiya hai.
trick: Agar 'Having + V3' se start karein, toh check karein ki agla word supreme court hai ya tech giants.
tip: Dangling modifier tab banta hai jab action aur doer match na karein.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The nation's foreign exchange reserves plummeted drastically. || II. The central bank was forced to devalue the fiat currency. || Starters: A. Plummeting drastically... B. Forced to devalue the fiat... C. Having forced to devalue... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'Plummeting drastically, the nation's foreign exchange reserves forced the central bank to devalue the currency.' 2) 'Forced to devalue the fiat currency, the central bank reacted to the plummeting reserves.' Starter C galat hai kyunki wahan 'Having been forced' aana chahiye tha. 'Having forced' active voice hai jiska matlab bank ne kisi aur ko force kiya.
trick: Hamesha dhyan dein ki 'forced' passive state hai, isliye iske aage 'been' lagna zaruri hai agar 'having' use ho.
tip: V3 (past participle) se start hone wale sentences hamesha passive hote hain.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The healthcare infrastructure was completely overwhelmed by the pandemic. || II. The federal government sought urgent international medical assistance. || Starters: A. Completely overwhelmed by the pandemic... B. Seeking urgent international medical... C. Having completely overwhelmed... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'Completely overwhelmed by the pandemic, the healthcare infrastructure prompted the federal government to seek assistance.' 2) 'Seeking urgent international medical assistance, the federal government responded to the overwhelmed infrastructure.' Starter C ek active trap hai; pandemic ne overwhelm kiya, infrastructure ne nahi.
trick: Elimination simple hai: Starter C active dikha raha hai ('Having overwhelmed'), jo ki context ke bilkul opposite hai.
tip: Contextual logic hamesha grammar rules ke sath check karein.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The controversial farm bills were repealed after prolonged protests. || II. The protesting farmers finally vacated the national highways. || Starters: A. Repealed after prolonged protests... B. Having repealed the controversial... C. After the controversial farm bills... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'Repealed after prolonged protests, the controversial farm bills led the farmers to vacate the highways.' 2) 'After the controversial farm bills were repealed, the protesting farmers finally vacated the highways.' Starter B galat hai kyunki farmers ne bills repeal nahi kiye the (dangling modifier).
trick: Starter B active action dikhata hai. Kya farmers ne khud laws repeal kiye? Nahi. Toh ye galat hai.
tip: Subject match karna sabse zaroori hai participle starters mein.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The electric vehicle subsidies were heavily slashed by the ministry. || II. The quarterly sales of major EV manufacturers saw a steep decline. || Starters: A. Slashing the electric vehicle... B. Having been heavily slashed... C. As a result of the heavy slashing... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'Having been heavily slashed by the ministry, the electric vehicle subsidies caused a steep decline in quarterly sales.' 2) 'As a result of the heavy slashing of subsidies, the quarterly sales saw a steep decline.' Starter A galat hai kyunki EV manufacturers ne subsidies slash nahi ki thi.
trick: Starter A se sentence shuru karne par agla subject EV manufacturers hoga, jo logically galat hai.
tip: Dependent clause ka doer independent clause ke subject jaisa hona chahiye.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The cyber security breach compromised millions of user accounts. || II. The tech startup faced a massive class-action lawsuit. || Starters: A. Compromising millions of user accounts... B. In the aftermath of the cyber security... C. Faced with a massive class-action... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'In the aftermath of the cyber security breach compromising millions of accounts, the tech startup faced a lawsuit.' 2) 'Faced with a massive class-action lawsuit, the tech startup suffered from the cyber security breach.' Starter A trap hai kyunki agar lawsuit subject banega toh matlab nikalta hai ki lawsuit ne accounts compromise kiye.
trick: Jab do alag-alag subjects ho (breach aur startup), toh prepositional phrase (Starter B) sabse safe bet hota hai.
tip: Prepositions cause aur effect ko safely link karne mein madad karte hain.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The global crude oil prices surged beyond the critical threshold. || II. The domestic transportation costs escalated rapidly. || Starters: A. Surging beyond the critical threshold... B. Having escalated rapidly... C. With the global crude oil prices... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'Surging beyond the critical threshold, the global crude oil prices caused domestic transportation costs to escalate.' 2) 'With the global crude oil prices surging beyond the critical threshold, domestic costs escalated.' Starter B ulta cause-effect dikhata hai, jaise transportation costs escalate hone ki wajah se oil prices badhe hon.
trick: Sequence of events hamesha barkarar rehni chahiye. Jo kaam pehle hua, wahi participle ka hissa banega.
tip: Chronological order ko participles mein reverse mat hone dein.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The municipal corporation neglected the underground drainage system. || II. The city experienced severe waterlogging during the monsoons. || Starters: A. Having neglected the underground... B. Experiencing severe waterlogging... C. Neglecting the severe waterlogging... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'Having neglected the underground drainage system, the municipal corporation was blamed for the severe waterlogging.' 2) 'Experiencing severe waterlogging during the monsoons, the city suffered due to the municipal corporation's neglect.' Starter C meaning ko distort kar deta hai (corporation ne drainage neglect kiya tha, waterlogging nahi).
trick: Starter C mein original sentence ka object (drainage system) gayab kar diya gaya hai, isliye wo eliminate ho jayega.
tip: Original sentences ka basic meaning kabhi modify nahi hona chahiye.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The primary school curriculum was updated to include digital literacy. || II. The students showed remarkable improvement in analytical skills. || Starters: A. Updated to include digital literacy... B. Showing remarkable improvement in... C. Having updated to include... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'Updated to include digital literacy, the primary school curriculum helped students show remarkable improvement.' 2) 'Showing remarkable improvement in analytical skills, the students benefited from the updated curriculum.' Starter C mein 'been' missing hai, isliye wo grammatically incorrect aur dangling trap ban gaya hai.
trick: 'Having updated' active hai jiska matlab curriculum ne khud ko update kiya. 'Having been updated' sahi hota.
tip: Non-living subjects ke sath hamesha passive participle ('been') dhundhein.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The diplomatic talks between the two neighboring nations collapsed. || II. The border security forces were put on high alert. || Starters: A. Following the collapse of the... B. Having collapsed between the two... C. Putting on high alert... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'Following the collapse of the diplomatic talks, the border security forces were put on high alert.' 2) 'Having collapsed between the two nations, the diplomatic talks led to the security forces being put on high alert.' Starter C active hone ke karan galat hai (forces ne khud ko alert par nahi rakha).
trick: Starter A jisme preposition 'Following' use hua hai, wo sabse safe aur universally correct combination method hai.
tip: Preposition-based starters dangling modifier ka risk khatam kar dete hain.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The foreign direct investment rules were significantly relaxed. || II. Several multinational corporations expanded their operations in the country. || Starters: A. Significantly relaxing the foreign... B. With the significant relaxation of... C. Having relaxed the foreign... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentence: 'With the significant relaxation of the foreign direct investment rules, several multinational corporations expanded their operations.' Starters A aur C dono dangling modifiers hain kyunki unhe sentence ke aage lagane se meaning aayega ki MNCs ne khud rules relax kiye hain.
trick: Jab pehla sentence pure passive ho aur doer (kisne relax kiya) missing ho, toh Noun phrase ('With the relaxation') hi best hota hai.
tip: Missing doer wale sentences mein noun phrase starters choose karein.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The pharmaceutical company failed the stringent quality control test. || II. The international health agency banned its entire product line. || Starters: A. Failing the stringent quality... B. Having been failed by the... C. Following the failure of the... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'Failing the stringent quality control test, the pharmaceutical company faced a ban from the health agency.' 2) 'Following the failure of the company in the quality test, the health agency banned its products.' Starter B grammatically weird hai aur original meaning change kar raha hai.
trick: Starter A seedha company ko refer karta hai (jisne fail kiya), isliye wo bilkul correct active participle hai.
tip: Active participle V+ing sahi hai agar action karne wala clear ho.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The ambitious space mission faced multiple technical glitches. || II. The space agency decided to postpone the lunar landing indefinitely. || Starters: A. Facing multiple technical glitches... B. Having decided to postpone... C. Decided to postpone... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'Facing multiple technical glitches, the ambitious space mission forced the agency to postpone the landing.' 2) 'Having decided to postpone the lunar landing indefinitely, the space agency reacted to the multiple technical glitches.' Starter C grammatically incomplete hai kyunki wo as a standalone valid starter act nahi kar sakta.
trick: V3 ('Decided') akele bina 'Having' ya subject ke aage nahi aa sakta jab wo active decision ko dikha raha ho.
tip: Participle phrases ko hamesha proper structure ('Having + V3') chahiye.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The new tax regime was implemented hastily. || II. Small businesses faced significant compliance burdens. || Starters: A. Having implemented hastily... B. Following the hasty implementation of... C. Facing significant compliance burdens... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'Following the hasty implementation of the new tax regime, small businesses faced significant compliance burdens.' 2) 'Facing significant compliance burdens, small businesses struggled because the new tax regime was implemented hastily.' Agar hum Starter A ('Having implemented hastily') use karte hain, toh lagta hai ki small businesses ne tax regime khud implement kiya, jo logically galat hai (dangling modifier).
trick: Starter A active voice mein hai. Implement sarkar ne kiya tha, businesses ne nahi, isliye eliminate karein.
tip: Dangling modifiers hamesha check karein: Participle ke baad doer match hona chahiye.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The subsidy burden widened the fiscal deficit. || II. The government decided to disinvest from loss-making PSUs. || Starters: A. Widening the fiscal deficit... B. Burdened by the widening fiscal deficit... C. Deciding to disinvest from... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'Burdened by the widening fiscal deficit due to subsidies, the government decided to disinvest from loss-making PSUs.' 2) 'Deciding to disinvest from loss-making PSUs, the government reacted to the widening fiscal deficit.' Starter A galat hai kyunki 'Widening the fiscal deficit' ke baad government aayega, jiska matlab hoga sarkar khud deficit widen kar rahi thi.
trick: Starter A lagane se action ka doer badal jayega. Cause (subsidy) aur effect (disinvestment) ka relation clear hona chahiye.
tip: Cause-effect sentences mein active/passive voice dhyan se padhein.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The appellate tribunal stayed the insolvency proceedings. || II. The corporate promoters breathed a sigh of relief. || Starters: A. Having been stayed by the... B. With the appellate tribunal staying... C. Breathing a sigh of relief... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'With the appellate tribunal staying the insolvency proceedings, the corporate promoters breathed a sigh of relief.' 2) 'Breathing a sigh of relief, the corporate promoters welcomed the appellate tribunal's stay.' Starter A ('Having been stayed') galat hai kyunki uske aage promoters aayega, toh lagta hai promoters ko stay kiya gaya, proceedings ko nahi.
trick: Starter A passive hai. Kya promoters stay huye the? Nahi. Proceeding stay hui thi. Toh A galat hai.
tip: 'With + Noun + Participle' hamesha safe absolute phrase banata hai.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The crypto assets are completely unregulated in the country. || II. Retail investors are highly vulnerable to market manipulation. || Starters: A. Being completely unregulated... B. As the crypto assets are... C. Highly vulnerable to market... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'As the crypto assets are completely unregulated, retail investors are highly vulnerable.' 2) 'Highly vulnerable to market manipulation, retail investors suffer because crypto assets are unregulated.' Starter A ('Being completely unregulated') ek dangling trap hai kyunki sentence retail investors se shuru hoga, jiska matlab nikalta hai ki investors unregulated hain, crypto nahi.
trick: 'Being + Adjective' usi subject ko refer karta hai jo main clause mein pehle aata hai. Yahan crypto unregulated hai.
tip: 'Being' wale starters mein main subject ka dhyaan rakhna zaroori hai.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The global supply chains were severely disrupted by geopolitical tensions. || II. The domestic auto sector struggled to procure semiconductor chips. || Starters: A. Severely disrupted by geopolitical... B. Struggling to procure semiconductor... C. Having severely disrupted the... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentence: 'Struggling to procure semiconductor chips, the domestic auto sector faced issues due to disrupted supply chains.' Starter A galat hai kyunki uske baad 'auto sector' aayega, aur lagta hai auto sector disrupt hua tha, jabki supply chain disrupt hui thi. Starter C active hone ki wajah se galat hai.
trick: Agar main subject 'auto sector' hai, toh wahi participle aayega jo auto sector ka action ('struggling') bataye.
tip: Jo sentence ka actual doer hai, usi ka action starter banega.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The antitrust watchdog penalized the tech behemoth heavily. || II. Several start-ups praised the landmark ruling publicly. || Starters: A. Penalizing the tech behemoth... B. Having been penalized heavily... C. Praising the landmark ruling... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentence: 'Praising the landmark ruling publicly, several start-ups welcomed the penalty on the tech behemoth.' Starter A galat hai kyunki startups ne tech behemoth ko penalize nahi kiya (dangling modifier). Starter B bhi galat hai kyunki startups penalize nahi hue the.
trick: Sentence ka naya subject hamesha 'start-ups' hoga. Start-ups ne na toh penalize kiya (A) na penalize hue (B).
tip: Action karne wala aur subject hamesha same hone chahiye.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The monsoon deficit threatened the Kharif crop yield. || II. The state authorities announced a contingency irrigation plan. || Starters: A. Threatened by the monsoon deficit... B. Threatening the Kharif crop... C. Announcing a contingency irrigation... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'Threatened by the monsoon deficit, the Kharif crop yield forced the authorities to announce a plan.' 2) 'Announcing a contingency irrigation plan, the state authorities reacted to the monsoon deficit.' Starter B galat hai kyunki 'Threatening' se shuru hone par lagta hai authorities crop ko threaten kar rahi hain.
trick: Starter B lagane par agla word 'authorities' hoga. Kya authorities crop threaten kar rahi hain? Nahi. Toh eliminate karein.
tip: Hamesha check karein 'Kaun kar raha hai ye action?'

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The municipal bonds received a lukewarm response from retail investors. || II. The civic body had to rely on institutional funding. || Starters: A. Having received a lukewarm... B. Relying on institutional funding... C. Due to the lukewarm response... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'Relying on institutional funding, the civic body managed after the municipal bonds received a lukewarm response.' 2) 'Due to the lukewarm response from retail investors to the municipal bonds, the civic body had to rely on institutional funding.' Starter A galat hai kyunki 'Having received' civic body par apply hoga, jabki bonds ne response receive kiya tha.
trick: Prepositional phrases ('Due to') sentences ko bina doer mismatch ke safely combine karte hain.
tip: Prepositions jodne ke sabse safe tools hote hain grammar mein.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The core inflation remained stubbornly above the tolerance band. || II. The monetary policy committee maintained a hawkish stance. || Starters: A. Remaining stubbornly above the... B. Maintaining a hawkish stance... C. With the core inflation remaining... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'Maintaining a hawkish stance, the monetary policy committee reacted to the core inflation.' 2) 'With the core inflation remaining above the tolerance band, the committee maintained a hawkish stance.' Starter A galat hai kyunki uske turant baad committee aayega, toh lagta hai committee inflation band ke upar thi.
trick: Starter A dangling modifier banata hai. 'Remaining' committee par apply nahi ho sakta, sirf inflation par ho sakta hai.
tip: Dangling modifier context aur logic ko poori tarah bigaad deta hai.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The free-trade agreement was successfully negotiated after five years. || II. The textile exporters anticipated a massive boost in overseas orders. || Starters: A. Having been successfully negotiated... B. Anticipating a massive boost... C. Following the successful negotiation... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'Anticipating a massive boost in overseas orders, the textile exporters celebrated the free-trade agreement.' 2) 'Following the successful negotiation of the free-trade agreement, textile exporters anticipated a boost.' Starter A galat hai kyunki 'Having been negotiated' textile exporters ke liye dangling ban jata hai (exporters negotiate nahi hue the).
trick: Starter A use karne se exporters khud negotiated lagte hain, jo ki senseless hai. Isko eliminate kardo.
tip: Noun phrase starters ('Following the negotiation') subject confusion mitate hain.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The legacy telecom operators accumulated massive adjusted gross revenue dues. || II. The sector stood on the brink of a duopoly. || Starters: A. Having accumulated massive adjusted... B. Standing on the brink of... C. Accumulated massive adjusted gross... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'Having accumulated massive adjusted gross revenue dues, the legacy telecom operators pushed the sector to the brink of a duopoly.' 2) 'Standing on the brink of a duopoly, the telecom sector suffered because of the massive accumulated dues.' Starter C grammatically incorrect past participle hai jiska yahan proper independent support nahi hai.
trick: 'Having + V3' (Starter A) ek perfect participle hai jo bilkul sahi hai kyunki operators ne dues accumulate kiye hain.
tip: 'Having + V3' dikhata hai ek action puri tarah pehle hi ho chuka hai.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The privatization drive faced stiff resistance from trade unions. || II. The divestment targets for the fiscal year were quietly revised. || Starters: A. Facing stiff resistance from... B. Quietly revised for the fiscal... C. Having faced stiff resistance... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'Facing stiff resistance from trade unions, the privatization drive led to the revision of divestment targets.' 2) 'Having faced stiff resistance, the privatization drive forced the revision of targets.' Starter B galat hai kyunki 'Quietly revised' ek passive participle hai jo directly kisi doer (sarkar) ko clearly point nahi kar raha in combination.
trick: 'Facing' present continuous context dikhata hai, jabki 'Having faced' past completion. Dono privatization drive ke liye valid hain.
tip: Context ke hisaab se Present ya Perfect participle use kiya ja sakta hai.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The renewable energy targets were upgraded significantly. || II. The power ministry rolled out massive production-linked incentives. || Starters: A. Upgrading the renewable energy... B. Rolling out massive production-linked... C. To upgrade the renewable energy... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'Rolling out massive production-linked incentives, the power ministry responded to the upgraded targets.' 2) 'To meet the significantly upgraded renewable energy targets, the power ministry rolled out incentives.' Starter A dangling trap hai kyunki ministry ne khud targets upgrade nahi kiye (they 'were upgraded' - passive).
trick: Infinitive 'To upgrade' (Starter C) ek future purpose dikhata hai, jo cause and action ko perfectly explain karta hai.
tip: Infinitive phrases 'why' ka jawaab dete hain ('kyun incentives diye?').

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The systemic risk was ignored by the credit rating agencies. || II. The shadow banking crisis eventually engulfed the entire financial sector. || Starters: A. Ignored by the credit rating... B. Engulfing the entire financial... C. Having been ignored by... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'Ignored by the credit rating agencies, the systemic risk caused the crisis.' 2) 'Engulfing the entire financial sector, the shadow banking crisis was a result of ignored risks.' 3) 'Having been ignored by the agencies, the systemic risk resulted in a crisis.' Yahan teeno perfectly fit baithte hain depending on main subject.
trick: Agar V3 (Ignored) aur 'Having been V3' dono hain, toh mostly dono sahi hote hain kyunki dono passive modifiers hain.
tip: Passive participles hamesha receiver of the action (risk) ko describe karte hain.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The strict environmental norms were abruptly relaxed by the ministry. || II. The coastal infrastructure projects gained immediate momentum. || Starters: A. Abruptly relaxing the strict... B. With the abrupt relaxation of... C. Gaining immediate momentum... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'With the abrupt relaxation of the strict environmental norms, the coastal infrastructure projects gained immediate momentum.' 2) 'Gaining immediate momentum, the coastal infrastructure projects benefited from the relaxed norms.' Starter A galat hai kyunki infrastructure projects ne khud norms relax nahi kiye the.
trick: Starter A active verb 'relaxing' dikhata hai. Jinhone norms relax kiye (ministry) wo main subject nahi hain, toh ye galat hoga.
tip: Subject-verb ka mismatch MCQ options me sabse bada elimination tool hai.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The demographic dividend remains largely underutilized. || II. The economy struggles to create adequate formal sector jobs. || Starters: A. Remaining largely underutilized... B. Struggling to create adequate... C. Because of the largely underutilized... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'Remaining largely underutilized, the demographic dividend poses a challenge as the economy struggles to create jobs.' 2) 'Struggling to create adequate formal sector jobs, the economy leaves the demographic dividend underutilized.' 3) 'Because of the largely underutilized demographic dividend, the economy struggles...' Teeno different grammatical structures se perfectly join hote hain.
trick: Conjunctions ('Because of') dono clauses ke beech relation directly establish kar dete hain bina modifier trap ke.
tip: Meaning maintain hona chahiye, chahe sentence active ho ya passive.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The aggressive pricing strategy eroded the profit margins. || II. The e-commerce giant reported its first-ever quarterly loss. || Starters: A. Eroding the profit margins... B. Having eroded the profit... C. Reporting its first-ever quarterly... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'Eroding the profit margins, the aggressive pricing strategy led the e-commerce giant to report a loss.' 2) 'Reporting its first-ever quarterly loss, the e-commerce giant suffered due to its aggressive pricing strategy.' Starter B ek imperfect match hai kyunki 'Having eroded' giant par directly apply hone par meaning distort karta hai.
trick: Participle phrases cause and effect ka order natural rakhte hain. A cause hai, C effect hai.
tip: Present participle ('V+ing') do simultaneous events ko badhiya connect karta hai.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The sovereign credit rating was downgraded by a major agency. || II. The foreign portfolio investors aggressively pulled out their capital. || Starters: A. Downgrading the sovereign credit... B. Having been downgraded by... C. Triggered by the downgrade of... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentence: 'Triggered by the downgrade of the sovereign credit rating, foreign portfolio investors aggressively pulled out their capital.' Starter A aur B dono investors par apply honge aur lagaga ki investors ne credit rating downgrade ki hai (dangling trap), jabki rating agencies ne ki thi.
trick: 'Having been downgraded' ka main subject investors banega, jo illogical hai. Pura passive galat ho jata hai.
tip: Participle kis noun ko modify kar raha hai, wahi error ki jadh hai.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The obsolete data protection laws failed to penalize the offenders. || II. The parliament rushed to draft a comprehensive privacy bill. || Starters: A. Failing to penalize the offenders... B. Rushing to draft a comprehensive... C. Having failed to penalize... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'Failing to penalize the offenders, the obsolete data protection laws prompted the parliament to act.' 2) 'Rushing to draft a comprehensive privacy bill, the parliament reacted to the obsolete laws.' 3) 'Having failed to penalize the offenders, the obsolete laws were replaced by the parliament.' Teeno logically aur grammatically valid hain.
trick: Jab dono subjects active state mein hon (laws failed, parliament rushed), toh participles easily swap ho sakte hain.
tip: Dono actions ka doer agar clear ho toh V-ing starters correct hote hain.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The aggressive interest rate hikes triggered a liquidity squeeze. || II. Several debt-laden real estate developers filed for bankruptcy. || Starters: A. Triggering a liquidity squeeze... B. Filing for bankruptcy... C. As a consequence of the liquidity... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'Triggering a liquidity squeeze, the aggressive interest rate hikes forced developers into bankruptcy.' 2) 'Filing for bankruptcy, several debt-laden developers became victims of the rate hikes.' 3) 'As a consequence of the liquidity squeeze triggered by rate hikes, developers filed for bankruptcy.'
trick: 'As a consequence of' (Starter C) ek cause-effect connector hai, aur pehle dono participles doers (hikes, developers) se clearly linked hain.
tip: Causal conjunctions combined sentences mein logical relation strong karte hain.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The central bank aggressively intervened in the forex market. || II. The national currency stabilized against the dollar. || Starters: A. Having aggressively intervened... B. Intervening aggressively in the... C. With the central bank aggressively intervening... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentence: 'With the central bank aggressively intervening in the forex market, the national currency stabilized against the dollar.' Agar hum Starter A ya B use karte hain, toh sentence ka naya subject 'national currency' ban jayega, jiska matlab nikalta hai ki currency ne forex market mein intervene kiya. Ye ek classic dangling modifier trap hai.
trick: Starter C ek absolute phrase hai jo dono alag-alag subjects (bank aur currency) ko bina unka meaning badle perfectly connect karta hai.
tip: Jab dono sentences ke subjects alag hon, toh 'With + Noun' ka use safe hai.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The infrastructure bill was stalled in the upper house. || II. The foreign investors withheld their capital allocations. || Starters: A. Having stalled the infrastructure... B. Stalled in the upper house... C. Because the infrastructure bill was... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentence: 'Because the infrastructure bill was stalled in the upper house, the foreign investors withheld their capital allocations.' Starter A galat hai kyunki investors ne bill stall nahi kiya tha. Starter B bhi galat hai kyunki use sentence ke aage lagane se lagta hai ki foreign investors upper house mein stall ho gaye the (dangling modifier).
trick: Starter B (V3 form) us subject ko modify karta hai jo turant uske baad aata hai. Yahan investors stall nahi huye, isliye B eliminate ho jayega.
tip: Passive participles hamesha us noun se jude hote hain jo action receive karta hai.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The minimum support price was hiked marginally. || II. The farmers intensified their nationwide agitation. || Starters: A. Having hiked the minimum... B. Infuriated by the marginal hike... C. With the minimum support price... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'Infuriated by the marginal hike in the minimum support price, the farmers intensified their agitation.' 2) 'With the minimum support price hiked marginally, the farmers intensified their nationwide agitation.' Starter A galat hai kyunki uske hisaab se farmers ne khud MSP hike kiya tha, jo context ke bilkul opposite hai.
trick: Starter A active voice ('Having hiked') mein hai. Hike sarkar ne kiya tha, isliye farmers ke sath ye starter match nahi karega.
tip: Subject ka doer hona zaroori hai agar active participle starter use ho.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The new privacy policy drew severe backlash from users. || II. The social media giant rolled back the controversial update. || Starters: A. Drawing severe backlash... B. Having drawn severe backlash... C. Rolled back by the social... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'Drawing severe backlash from users, the new privacy policy was rolled back by the social media giant.' 2) 'Having drawn severe backlash from users, the new privacy policy forced the social media giant to roll back the update.' Starter C galat hai kyunki 'Rolled back' lagane par agla word privacy policy hoga, jiska matlab nikalta hai ki policy ne kisi aur cheez ko roll back kiya.
trick: A aur B dono 'privacy policy' ke action (backlash draw karna) ko describe karte hain, isliye dono sahi hain.
tip: V+ing aur Having+V3 dono same subject ke continuous ya completed actions hain.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The coal reserves depleted to alarmingly low levels. || II. Several thermal power plants shut down operations. || Starters: A. Depleting to alarmingly low... B. Having shut down operations... C. Due to the depletion of... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'Having shut down operations, several thermal power plants reacted to the depleted coal reserves.' 2) 'Due to the depletion of coal reserves, several thermal power plants shut down operations.' Starter A galat hai kyunki 'Depleting' ke baad power plants aayega, jiska matlab nikalta hai ki power plants khud deplete ho rahe the.
trick: Starter A ek dangling modifier banata hai. 'Deplete' reserves huye hain, power plants nahi. Logical connection check karein.
tip: Hamesha check karein: Participle ke baad aane wala Noun action kar raha hai ya nahi.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The geopolitical tensions escalated in the Middle East. || II. The global supply chains suffered massive disruptions. || Starters: A. Escalating in the Middle East... B. With geopolitical tensions escalating... C. Having suffered massive disruptions... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'With geopolitical tensions escalating in the Middle East, the global supply chains suffered massive disruptions.' 2) 'Having suffered massive disruptions, the global supply chains were impacted by the escalating tensions.' Starter A dangling modifier hai kyunki supply chains Middle East mein escalate nahi ho rahi thi.
trick: Starter C perfectly 'supply chains' ko modify kar raha hai (kyunki disruptions unhi ko hui thi), aur B ek absolute phrase hai.
tip: Absolute phrases ('With + noun + V-ing') cause batane ke liye best hote hain.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The corporate tax rate was slashed to boost manufacturing. || II. The fiscal deficit widened beyond permissible limits. || Starters: A. Slashed to boost manufacturing... B. Having slashed the corporate... C. While the corporate tax rate... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentence: 'While the corporate tax rate was slashed to boost manufacturing, the fiscal deficit widened beyond permissible limits.' Starter A galat hai kyunki uske aage 'fiscal deficit' aayega (matlab deficit slash hua tha, jo galat hai). Starter B active hai, jiska matlab nikalta hai deficit ne tax slash kiya.
trick: Dono alag-alag subjects hain (tax rate aur fiscal deficit). Aise mein Participle starters (A aur B) hamesha dangling trap banate hain.
tip: Dangling modifiers se bachne ke liye Conjunctions ('While', 'As') ka use sabse accha hai.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The regulatory framework was thoroughly revamped by the committee. || II. The fintech startups found it easier to secure licenses. || Starters: A. Thoroughly revamped by the committee... B. Having been thoroughly revamped... C. Finding it easier to secure... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentence: 'Finding it easier to secure licenses, the fintech startups benefited after the regulatory framework was revamped.' Starters A aur B dono passive participles hain jo framework ke liye hain. Agar inko aage lagayenge, toh agla word 'startups' aayega, jiska matlab nikalta hai startups revamp huye the.
trick: A aur B lagane se startups 'thoroughly revamp' ho jayenge, jo meaning completely badal deta hai. Sirf C startups ke action ko batata hai.
tip: Startups subject hain, toh starter wahi hoga jo startups ka action bataye.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The unprecedented heatwave destroyed the standing wheat crop. || II. The government imposed a ban on agricultural exports. || Starters: A. Destroying the standing wheat... B. Having destroyed the standing... C. Faced with the destruction of... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentence: 'Faced with the destruction of the standing wheat crop by the heatwave, the government imposed a ban on agricultural exports.' Starter A aur B active participles hain jo destruction dikhate hain. Agar inko government ke aage lagaya jaye, toh meaning aayega ki sarkar ne crop destroy kiya.
trick: Kya sarkar ne fasal kharab ki? Nahi. Heatwave ne ki. Toh 'Destroying' aur 'Having destroyed' dono eliminate ho jayenge.
tip: Aisa starter choose karein jiska meaning main subject ke sath logically baithe.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The retail inflation breached the upper tolerance limit. || II. The monetary policy committee convened an emergency meeting. || Starters: A. Breaching the upper tolerance... B. Having breached the upper... C. Convening an emergency meeting... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentence: 'Convening an emergency meeting, the monetary policy committee reacted to the retail inflation breaching the limit.' Starters A aur B dono inflation ke actions hain. Inko committee ke aage lagane se lagta hai ki committee ne limit breach ki hai (dangling trap).
trick: Main clause ka subject hamesha 'committee' hoga, isliye starter bhi wahi hona chahiye jo committee ka action ('Convening') dikhaye.
tip: Participle starter aur Sentence ke main subject ka action match hona chahiye.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The apex court mandated the immediate demolition of the illegal towers. || II. The municipal body deployed heavy machinery to the site. || Starters: A. Mandated by the apex court... B. Following the apex court's mandate... C. Deploying heavy machinery... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'Following the apex court's mandate, the municipal body deployed heavy machinery.' 2) 'Deploying heavy machinery to the site, the municipal body acted on the apex court's mandate.' Starter A galat hai kyunki 'Mandated' towers ke liye tha, municipal body ke liye nahi.
trick: Starter A se shuru karne par lagta hai municipal body demolish hone wali hai, jo absurd hai. C aur B safe connections hain.
tip: Prepositional phrases ('Following') logic ko preserve karte hain.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The semiconductor shortage crippled the automobile industry. || II. The leading car manufacturers suspended production temporarily. || Starters: A. Crippled by the semiconductor shortage... B. Suspending production temporarily... C. Having crippled the automobile... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'Crippled by the semiconductor shortage, the leading car manufacturers suspended production.' 2) 'Suspending production temporarily, the leading car manufacturers reacted to the shortage.' Starter C galat hai kyunki manufacturers ne industry ko cripple nahi kiya tha (shortage ne kiya tha).
trick: Starter C use karne se active doer 'manufacturers' ban jate hain crippling ke liye, jo bilkul logically ulta hai.
tip: 'V-ing' aur 'V-ed' dono sahi ho sakte hain agar wo same subject ko modify karein.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The public sector banks were merged to create larger entities. || II. The operational efficiency improved drastically over the year. || Starters: A. Merged to create larger... B. Having been merged to... C. With the public sector banks being... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentence: 'With the public sector banks being merged to create larger entities, the operational efficiency improved drastically.' Starters A aur B ko agar 'operational efficiency' ke aage lagaya jaye, toh lagta hai efficiency merge ho gayi thi (dangling modifier).
trick: Efficiency merge nahi hui, banks merge huye. Isliye banks ka subject clear hona zaroori hai, jo sirf Starter C mein hai.
tip: 'With' se shuru hone wale starters independent clauses ko safely jodte hain.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The bilateral trade talks reached a sudden deadlock. || II. The diplomatic envoys returned to their respective capitals. || Starters: A. Reaching a sudden deadlock... B. Having reached a sudden deadlock... C. As the bilateral trade talks... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentence: 'As the bilateral trade talks reached a sudden deadlock, the diplomatic envoys returned to their respective capitals.' Starters A aur B ka doer 'diplomatic envoys' ban jayega jiska matlab nikalta hai envoys deadlock ban gaye, jabki deadlock talks mein aaya tha.
trick: A aur B dono dangling traps hain. Participle us cheez ko dhoondhta hai jo immediately comma ke baad aati hai (Envoys).
tip: Dangling modifiers ka basic rule: Starter aur main subject ka logical link check karein.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The artificial intelligence tools became highly sophisticated. || II. Many traditional entry-level jobs were rendered obsolete. || Starters: A. Becoming highly sophisticated... B. Rendered obsolete by the... C. With the artificial intelligence tools... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'Rendered obsolete by the highly sophisticated artificial intelligence tools, many traditional entry-level jobs disappeared.' 2) 'With the artificial intelligence tools becoming highly sophisticated, entry-level jobs were rendered obsolete.' Starter A lagane se lagta hai ki 'jobs' sophisticated ban gayi, jo galat hai.
trick: Jobs sophisticated nahi huye (AI tools huye), isliye A galat hai. Jobs obsolete huye isliye B bilkul sahi passive starter hai.
tip: Identify karein ki sentence mein kaun change ho raha hai, wahi starter lega.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The state government allocated hefty funds for rural development. || II. The grassroots infrastructure witnessed a massive transformation. || Starters: A. Allocating hefty funds for... B. Having allocated hefty funds... C. Witnessing a massive transformation... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentence: 'Witnessing a massive transformation, the grassroots infrastructure benefited from the funds allocated by the state government.' Agar hum A ya B use karte hain toh lagta hai infrastructure ne khud funds allocate kiye hain, jo logically absurd hai.
trick: Main clause ka subject hamesha infrastructure hoga yahan. Infrastructure ne sirf 'witness' kiya hai, allocate nahi kiya.
tip: Aisa option hamesha eliminate karein jo subject-verb logic ko todta ho.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The strict lockdown protocols were enforced nationwide. || II. The daily wage laborers faced unprecedented economic hardships. || Starters: A. Enforcing strict lockdown protocols... B. Facing unprecedented economic hardships... C. Because of the strict lockdown... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'Facing unprecedented economic hardships, the daily wage laborers suffered as lockdown protocols were enforced.' 2) 'Because of the strict lockdown protocols enforced nationwide, the laborers faced hardships.' Starter A lagane se meaning aayega ki laborers khud protocols enforce kar rahe the.
trick: Laborers enforce nahi karte, wo suffer karte hain. 'Facing' unke liye perfect participle hai, aur 'Enforcing' trap hai.
tip: Active participle ('-ing') us subject ka action hona chahiye jo turant baad aata hai.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The generic drug makers bypassed the stringent patent laws. || II. The pharmaceutical giant filed a lawsuit in the international court. || Starters: A. Bypassing the stringent patent... B. Having bypassed the stringent... C. Filing a lawsuit in the... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentence: 'Filing a lawsuit in the international court, the pharmaceutical giant reacted to the generic drug makers bypassing patents.' Starters A aur B ko giant ke aage lagane se matlab niklega ki giant ne khud apne patent laws bypass kiye (jo ki generic makers ne kiye the).
trick: Patent laws bypass generic makers ne kiye the. Agar main subject 'pharmaceutical giant' hai, toh wo bypass wale participles nahi le sakta.
tip: Dangling modifiers hamesha ulta meaning create kar dete hain, dhyan se padhein.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The outdated labor laws were systematically repealed. || II. The foreign direct investment surged in the manufacturing hub. || Starters: A. Systematically repealed by the... B. Having systematically repealed the... C. Following the systematic repeal of... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentence: 'Following the systematic repeal of the outdated labor laws, the foreign direct investment surged in the manufacturing hub.' Starters A aur B ko agar 'FDI' ke aage lagayein toh matlab niklega ki FDI ko repeal kiya gaya (A) ya FDI ne khud laws repeal kiye (B). Dono senseless hain.
trick: 'Following' ek preposition hai jo laws ke repeal hone aur FDI badhne dono actions ko beautifully join kar deta hai bina koi dangling trap banaye.
tip: Preposition-based phrases ('Following', 'Due to') safe combiners hote hain.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The tech startup failed to secure the next round of funding. || II. The management announced mass layoffs. || Starters: A. Failing to secure the next... B. Having failed to secure the... C. Announcing mass layoffs... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'Failing to secure the next round of funding, the management announced mass layoffs.' 2) 'Having failed to secure funding, the management announced mass layoffs.' 3) 'Announcing mass layoffs, the management reacted to the failure to secure funding.' Yahan 'management' aur 'startup' ko ek hi entity mana ja sakta hai.
trick: Kyunki 'startup' aur 'management' essentially same organization ko refer karte hain, teeno participles naturally aur logically fit baithte hain.
tip: Jab do clauses ka subject same entity ho, toh active participles easily interchange ho sakte hain.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The non-performing assets of public sector banks declined significantly. || II. The credit growth in the corporate sector witnessed a robust rebound. || Starters: A. Declining significantly... B. With the non-performing assets... C. Having declined significantly... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentence: 'With the non-performing assets of public sector banks declining significantly, the credit growth in the corporate sector witnessed a robust rebound.' Agar hum Starter A ya C use karte hain, toh sentence ke baad 'credit growth' aayega. Iska matlab niklega ki 'credit growth' decline ho rahi thi, jo context ke bilkul opposite hai (dangling modifier).
trick: Jab dono sentences ke subjects alag-alag hon (NPAs aur credit growth), toh V+ing modifiers generally avoid karne chahiye. 'With + Noun' sabse safe hai.
tip: Alag subjects hone par absolute phrases ('With + noun') use karein.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The ambitious digital currency was rolled out in the pilot phase. || II. Commercial banks struggled to integrate the underlying blockchain framework. || Starters: A. Rolled out in the pilot... B. As the ambitious digital... C. Struggling to integrate the... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'As the ambitious digital currency was rolled out in the pilot phase, commercial banks struggled.' 2) 'Struggling to integrate the underlying blockchain framework, commercial banks faced issues after the digital currency was rolled out.' Starter A ek trap hai, kyunki 'Rolled out' ke aage 'commercial banks' aayega, matlab banks ko roll out kiya gaya tha.
trick: Starter C main subject 'commercial banks' ka action bata raha hai, isliye correct hai. Starter A dangling modifier ban jayega.
tip: Passive starter wahi noun lega jo action receive kar raha ho.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The sudden imposition of export duty on steel products triggered a market panic. || II. Major domestic steelmakers halted their expansion projects indefinitely. || Starters: A. Triggered by the sudden imposition... B. Halting their expansion projects... C. Having triggered a market panic... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'Triggered by the sudden imposition of export duty, major domestic steelmakers halted their projects.' 2) 'Halting their expansion projects indefinitely, major domestic steelmakers reacted to the export duty.' Starter C galat hai kyunki 'steelmakers' ne market panic trigger nahi kiya, duty imposition ne kiya.
trick: Starter C active state mein hai ('Having triggered'). Steelmakers main clause ka subject hain, par unhone panic trigger nahi kiya. Isliye C eliminate hoga.
tip: Karega wahi bharega: Participle action wahi karega jo subject hoga.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The comprehensive green hydrogen policy was approved by the union cabinet. || II. Several energy conglomerates announced massive investments in renewable infrastructure. || Starters: A. Approved by the union cabinet... B. Following the approval of the... C. Having approved the comprehensive... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentence: 'Following the approval of the comprehensive green hydrogen policy by the union cabinet, several energy conglomerates announced massive investments.' Starter A aur C dono dangling traps hain. Conglomerates na toh approve huye the (A) aur na hi unhone policy approve ki thi (C).
trick: Sentence II ka subject 'conglomerates' hai. Kya unhone policy approve ki? Nahi (sarkar ne ki). Toh A aur C reject ho gaye.
tip: Noun phrase starters ('Following...') se doer match karne ki tension khatam.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The foreign direct investment limit in the defense sector was raised to seventy-four percent. || II. Indigenous arms manufacturers formed joint ventures with global giants. || Starters: A. Raised to seventy-four percent... B. With the foreign direct investment... C. Forming joint ventures with... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'With the foreign direct investment limit raised, indigenous arms manufacturers formed joint ventures.' 2) 'Forming joint ventures with global giants, indigenous arms manufacturers capitalized on the raised FDI limit.' Starter A galat hai kyunki lagta hai 'manufacturers' ko 74 percent tak raise kiya gaya.
trick: Starter A (V3) ek passive action hai jo limit par apply hota hai, manufacturers par nahi. Isliye A ko eliminate karein.
tip: Sentence ka starting modifier aur comma ke baad ka noun match hona chahiye.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The aggressive monetary tightening cycle squeezed liquidity from the banking system. || II. Non-banking financial companies faced severe challenges in rolling over their debt. || Starters: A. Squeezed liquidity from the... B. Squeezing liquidity from the... C. Facing severe challenges in... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentence: 'Facing severe challenges in rolling over their debt, non-banking financial companies suffered as the tightening cycle squeezed liquidity.' Starter A grammatically galat phrase hai. Starter B dangling modifier hai kyunki NBFCs ne liquidity squeeze nahi ki thi, tightening cycle ne ki thi.
trick: Agar hum Starter B lagayenge toh matlab hoga NBFCs liquidity squeeze kar rahi hain. Jo ki completely ulta aur illogical hai.
tip: V+ing us subject ka action batata hai jo uske immediately baad aata hai.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The mandatory e-way bill generation system encountered a technical glitch. || II. Thousands of commercial transport vehicles were stranded at state borders. || Starters: A. Encountering a technical glitch... B. Stranded at state borders... C. Due to the technical glitch... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'Stranded at state borders, thousands of commercial transport vehicles suffered because of the glitch.' 2) 'Due to the technical glitch in the e-way bill system, thousands of vehicles were stranded.' Starter A dangling trap hai kyunki vehicles ne technical glitch encounter nahi kiya, system ne kiya.
trick: Starter A vehicles ke action ke roop mein dikhega. Kya gaadiyon ke andar glitch aaya? Nahi, portal mein aaya tha. Toh A eliminate.
tip: Context samjho: Action kon kar raha hai aur action kiske upar ho raha hai.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The government allocated an unprecedented budget for the semiconductor PLI scheme. || II. Global chipmakers showed immense interest in setting up domestic foundries. || Starters: A. Allocating an unprecedented budget... B. Showing immense interest in... C. Having allocated an unprecedented... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentence: 'Showing immense interest in setting up domestic foundries, global chipmakers reacted positively to the PLI scheme.' Starter A aur C dono active participles hain, lekin inka subject 'government' hai, 'chipmakers' nahi. Agar inhein aage lagaya toh meaning aayega ki chipmakers ne budget allocate kiya.
trick: Sentence ka combination 'global chipmakers' se shuru hoga. Unhone budget allocate nahi kiya, interest show kiya. Isliye A aur C reject honge.
tip: Modifier check karne ke liye apne aap se pucho: 'Ye kaam kisne kiya?'

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The windfall tax on crude oil production was abruptly slashed. || II. The stock prices of upstream exploration companies rallied sharply. || Starters: A. Abruptly slashed... B. Rallying sharply... C. Following the abrupt slashing... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'Rallying sharply, the stock prices of upstream exploration companies reacted to the slashed windfall tax.' 2) 'Following the abrupt slashing of the windfall tax, the stock prices rallied sharply.' Starter A galat hai kyunki 'stock prices' ko abruptly slash nahi kiya gaya tha, tax ko kiya gaya tha.
trick: Starter A (passive) us subject ke aage aana chahiye jo slash hua ho. Stock prices rally (badhe) huye hain, slash (ghate) nahi.
tip: Sentence mein positive aur negative growth verbs ka track rakhein.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The prolonged heatwave severely damaged the anticipated wheat harvest. || II. The commerce ministry imposed an immediate embargo on grain exports. || Starters: A. Severely damaging the anticipated... B. Imposing an immediate embargo... C. Having been severely damaged... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentence: 'Imposing an immediate embargo on grain exports, the commerce ministry reacted to the heatwave damaging the harvest.' Starter A galat hai kyunki commerce ministry ne fasal damage nahi ki. Starter C galat hai kyunki ministry ko damage nahi pahuncha (dangling modifiers).
trick: Main clause 'commerce ministry' se start hoga. Kya ministry ne fasal kharab ki (A)? Nahi. Kya ministry kharab hui (C)? Nahi. Sab eliminate.
tip: Subject aur participle ek doosre ke liye logically bane hone chahiye.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The reserve price for the 5G spectrum auction was deemed exorbitant by operators. || II. The bidding process witnessed a muted response in multiple circles. || Starters: A. Deemed exorbitant by operators... B. Witnessing a muted response... C. As the reserve price... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'Witnessing a muted response in multiple circles, the bidding process suffered because of the exorbitant reserve price.' 2) 'As the reserve price was deemed exorbitant, the bidding process witnessed a muted response.' Starter A galat hai kyunki 'bidding process' ko exorbitant (mehenga) nahi mana gaya, 'reserve price' ko mana gaya.
trick: Exorbitant (bohot mehenga) price hota hai, process nahi. Isliye Starter A bidding process ke aage dangling modifier ban jayega.
tip: Adjectives check karein ki kis noun ko naturally modify kar sakte hain.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The flat thirty percent tax on virtual digital assets deterred retail traders. || II. The daily trading volume on domestic crypto exchanges plummeted by seventy percent. || Starters: A. Deterring retail traders... B. Plummeting by seventy percent... C. Having deterred retail traders... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentence: 'Plummeting by seventy percent, the daily trading volume reacted to the thirty percent tax deterring retail traders.' Starter A aur C dono ka subject 'tax' hai. Agar unhein 'trading volume' ke aage lagaya jaye, toh meaning nikalta hai ki 'trading volume' ne traders ko deter (daraya) kiya, jo contextually weak hai.
trick: Traders ko tax ne daraya tha, volume ne nahi. Isliye 'Deterring' volume ke aage properly fit nahi baithega.
tip: Sentence combination original sentences ke cause-effect ko respect kare.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The prices of aviation turbine fuel soared to a record high. || II. Budget airlines were compelled to hike their passenger fares. || Starters: A. Soaring to a record high... B. Compelled to hike their... C. Having soared to a record... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentence: 'Compelled to hike their passenger fares, budget airlines reacted to the prices of aviation turbine fuel soaring to a record high.' Starter A aur C ka action 'soaring' hai (badhna). Agar ise airlines ke aage rakha jaye, toh lagta hai 'airlines' asmaan me record high udd rahi hain, jo literal meaning me galat ban jata hai (prices badhe the).
trick: Airlines nahi badhi, prices badhe hain. Isliye 'Soaring' seedha airlines ko describe nahi kar sakta (dangling trap).
tip: Dangling modifiers ka sabse accha ilaj: V-ing action ka real doer pehchano.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The implementation of the four new labor codes was deferred repeatedly. || II. Multi-national corporations hesitated to finalize their annual hiring plans. || Starters: A. Deferred repeatedly... B. Hesitating to finalize their... C. Because the implementation of... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'Hesitating to finalize their annual hiring plans, multi-national corporations waited due to the deferred labor codes.' 2) 'Because the implementation of the new labor codes was deferred, corporations hesitated.' Starter A galat hai kyunki 'corporations' ko defer nahi kiya gaya tha.
trick: Deferred ka matlab hota hai postopone hona. Kya MNCs postpone ho rahi thi? Nahi, policy ho rahi thi. Toh A reject ho jayega.
tip: Passive starter (V-ed) un nouns par apply na karein jo intentionally act karein.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. The import duty on unrefined edible oils was reduced to zero. || II. The domestic retail prices of essential cooking oils cooled down significantly. || Starters: A. Reduced to zero... B. With the import duty... C. Cooling down significantly... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'With the import duty reduced to zero, the domestic retail prices cooled down.' 2) 'Cooling down significantly, the domestic retail prices reacted to the zero import duty.' Starter A galat hai kyunki 'retail prices' zero nahi huye the, sirf duty zero hui thi.
trick: Prices kabhi directly zero nahi huye sentences mein. Isliye 'Reduced to zero' prices ke aage lagana logic ko break kar deta hai.
tip: Data points aur values (like 'zero') kis word ke liye hain, dhyaan dein.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I. Pivoting towards aggressive cost-cutting... C. Forced by the dried-up... || Question: Select the correct combination.
explanation: Combined sentences: 1) 'Pivoting towards aggressive cost-cutting measures, several unicorns reacted to the funding winter.' 2) 'Forced by the dried-up late-stage investments, several unicorns pivoted to cost-cutting.' Starter A dangling trap hai kyunki unicorns ne investments dry up nahi ki, funding winter ne ki thi.
trick: Starter A lagane se sentence batayega ki unicorns khud investments ko sukha rahe hain, jo unke nuksan mein hai. Logic eliminate karta hai isko.
tip: Business contexts mein cause (winter) aur effect (pivoting) hamesha distinct rakhein.

question: Direction: Which of the following phrases (A, B, C) can be used as a starter to combine the following sentences into one logically and grammatically correct sentence? || I.
